newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: EDP small investors seen gaining - president.
newsitem.headline: EDP small investors seen gaining - president.

text.p: Small investors in the partial privatisation of utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal should gain at least 20 percent on their investment in the first year, EDP president Antonio de Almeida said.

"With a six percent initial discount, plus four percent discount for those who hold the shares for the first 12 months, and another 10 percent discount in the privatisation price -- if small investors don't gain at least 20 percent in the first year, they have made a poor investment," Almeida said on the "Dinheiro Vivo" programme on RTP state television on Saturday.

Small investors in the privatisation of an expected 30 percent of EDP have the right to six percent discount on the fixed privatisation price which will be set later by the cabinet. Those small investors who hold their shares for a full year will gain one share for every 25 held, which means an additional four percent discount on their initial purchase. Furthermore, the privatisation price is expected to incorporate a discount as EDP has no previous history of trading on Lisbon bourse.
The public offer to sell (OPV) of EDP shares will take place on Lisbon bourse on June 16.
